newsitem.title: USA: Hyatt buys Trump's stake in Grand Hyatt New York.
newsitem.headline: Hyatt buys Trump's stake in Grand Hyatt New York.

text.p: Hyatt Corp, owned by the Pritzker family, said Monday it acquired Donald Trump's partnership interest in the 1,407-room Grand Hyatt New York, located in midtown Manhattan. Terms were not disclosed.
Hyatt Corp and an affiliate now own over 99 percent of the hotel, with the remainder owned by a Pritzker family philanthropic fund.

"The acquisition of our partner's interest in the Grand Hyatt New York reflects Hyatt's optimism in the hotel's future business prospects, as well as the overall vitality of the Manhattan hotel market," said Douglas Geoga, president of Hyatt Hotels, which manages the property.

Hyatt said the purchase of Trump's interest in the Grand Hyatt New York was part of the company's overall growth strategy. In the last several years, Hyatt and its affiliates have invested more than $500 million in acquiring and expanding Hyatt hotels and resorts.

The Grand Hyatt is currently undergoing a multi-million dollar renovation. In 1980, Grand Hyatt New York opened after a $100 million reconstruction of Manhattan's landmark Commodore Hotel, built in 1916. The property is adjacent to Grand Central Station.
